newsitem.title: UK: Large death tolls rare in air hijacking.
newsitem.headline: Large death tolls rare in air hijacking.

text.p: Saturday's hijacking of an Ethiopian Airlines passenger jet and its resulting crash in the Indian Ocean will go down as one of the deadliest episodes in the history of air piracy.
At least 50 people are reported dead but 45 of the Ethiopian plane's 175 passengers and crew are known to have survived its crash off the Comoro Islands.
The worst known crash resulting from hijacking killed 128 people in the Chinese city of Canton in October 1990.

Other hijackings which cost more than 50 deaths were an Egyptair plane stormed by Egyptian commandos in Malta in November 1985, with a toll of 59 dead, and an Air Vietnam brought down by a hijacker's hand grenades in September 1974 killing all 70 aboard.
The following is a list of some of the world's most noteworthy hijackings:
February, 1931 -- The first recorded hijacking of an airliner took place in Peru.

July, 1948 -- First hijacking in Asia, when a Cathay Pacific Catalina plane from Macao to Hong Kong was boarded by four Chinese hijackers. Pilot and co-pilot were killed and the plane crashed into the sea killing 25 aboard.
April, 1958 -- Start of the "Cuban shuttle". A Cubana airlines plane was flown to Mexico starting a two-way flow of hijacked planes between Cuba and the United States and Mexico.
August, 1960 -- First reported hijacking in the Soviet Union. Details were not released as Soviet data was secret.
July, 1968 - First Arab-Israeli incident and first in a series of political hijackings when three Arabs seized an El-Al Israeli plane in Rome and forced it to fly to Algiers.

September, 1970 - Palestinian guerrillas hijacked three airliners -- one TWA, one Swissair and one BOAC -- forcing them to land in Jordan where the planes were blown up. All hostages were released in exchange for Palestinan prisoners.
September, 1974 - Air Vietnam plane hijacked leaving Danang by a lone man demanding to go to Hanoi. Hijacker detonated two hand grenades; explosion and crash killed all 70 aboard.

July 1976 - Two Palestinians and two Europeans hijacked an Air France Airbus with 244 passengers and 12 crew to Entebbe in Uganda. They released 153 non-Jewish passengers and Israel staged a long-range rescue of the others.

February 1978 - Two Arab guerrillas seized an airliner at Larnaca, Cyprus. Egyptian commandos flew in uninvited to try to storm the plane during negotiations. Cyprus National Guardsmen resisted them and 15 Egyptians died in a 45-minute battle.
August 1980 - A total of 168 hijackers seized a Braniff airliner in Peru demanding to fly to Miami. After they gave up the United States agreed to expedite their emigration papers.
June 1985 -- Two Lebanese Shi'ite gunmen hijacked a TWA flight out of Athens with 153 aboard. Hijacking ended 16 days later at Beirut airport with one killed and 39 Americans freed.
November 1985 - Palestinians hijacked an Egyptair plane to Malta. Egyptian commandos stormed the plane and 59 people died.

September 5, 1986 - Twenty-two people died when Pakistani security forces stormed a Pan Am Boeing 747 carrying 400 passengers and crew to end a 16-hour siege which began after four Palestinian hijackers boarded at Karachi.

March 8, 1988 - Two members of a Siberian family pulled shotguns from musical instrument cases and demanded to be flown to London. The Tupolev 154 landed instead at a military airfield near Leningrad where nine people died when security forces stormed the plane.
April 5, 1988 - Arab gunmen seized a Kuwait Airways Boeing 747 carrying 115 passengers and killed two Kuwaitis. Hijack abandoned on April 20 in Algiers.
January 26, 1990 - Four gunmen tried to hijack an Iran Air Boeing 727 but were killed by security guards in a mid-air shootout over southern Iran.
August 20, 1990 - Eleven Soviet convicts surrendered to security forces after overpowering their guards and forcing an Aeroflot Tu-154 with 92 passengers and 9 crew to fly to Karachi.
October 2, 1990 - Hijackers seized a Chinese Airways Boeing 737 aircraft with 94 passengers and 10 crew after it left Xiamen but it crashed as it tried to land in Canton, killing 128.

October 10, 1990 - Two Burmese youths surrendered at Calcutta airport on November 11, 1990 after hijacking a Thai International Airways Airbus with 204 passengers and 17 crew to press demands for an end to military rule in their country.

March, 1991 - Four Pakistani hijackers seized a Singapore Air A310 Airbus on a flight to Singapore to demand the release of the husband of Benazir Bhutto, Asif Ali Zardari. Singaporean commandos stormed the plane with 114 passengers and nine crew and shot dead all four hijackers. Passengers and crew were safe.
March 18, 1993 - Security forces stormed a hijacked Ethiopian Airlines plane at Dire Dawa in eastern Ethiopia, killing two of four hijackers and a woman passenger.

October 25, 1993 - A Nigerian Airways Airbus 310 was hijacked on an internal flight and was forced to fly to Niamey, Niger, where 129 of the 149 passengers and crew were released. Niger security forces stormed the plane, freeing the passengers but killing one of the crew. The four hijackers were detained.

October 25, 1994 - Armed hijackers seized a Yak-40 passenger plane with 27 passengers on a flight to Rostov. Thirteen passengers were released at Makhachkala, Dagestan. Two dozen hostages were released after Russian authorities paid a ransom of $2.3 million. The hijacker blew himself up when police commandos stormed the plane. There were no other casualties.
